ForgeDoc Component Showcase & Verification Suite

This document exercises all 33 authored and child tags, so that a regression in any of them shows up in one test.

 Light DOM only — decided Runtime injected at build time Answer the questions inline, then send the bucket back Mermaid version pin still open

A component library for AI-authored planning documents. The agent writes semantic markup and nothing else — no <style>, no <script>, no class names, no section numbers. See for delivery order. Tagged as preview, stable, draft, deprecated, reference, and highlighted.

The runtime handles web components, persistence and feedback collection. A second mention of web components renders more quietly than the first.

Selection APIs do not cross shadow boundaries cleanly, and the feedback bucket lets a reader select arbitrary text anywhere in the document.

Every token is prefixed --doc-, so Mermaid and Prism cannot collide with it.

Table stacking below 1050px, which the reference document needs twice.

The validator and the three build variants ship from one source tree.

Never call attachShadow. A lint rule enforces it.

Depth two exists to prove the numbering. The number is at least as large as its heading and shrinks with depth.

Depth three is the deepest level the vocabulary supports.

    Two plans opened from disk see each other's answers, and one reader's feedback surfaces inside an unrelated document. Chrome has historically treated every file:// origin as one storage bucket. Every key is namespaced forgedoc:<doc-id>:state, and the validator rejects a document without a doc-id. A reader cannot copy "3.1" out of a heading. The numbering="text" attribute renders real text nodes instead. Bundling it into the CDN build punishes every reader. The full diagram registry ships as one module.
